newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says he should not act on UPS strike now.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says he should not act on UPS strike now.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said Monday he did not think it would be appropriate for him to intervene in the United Parcel Service strike now and he wanted the parties to return to the negotiating table.

"I still think the parties ought to go back to the table," Clinton told reporters during a White House event, noting his administration had sought the intervention of a federal mediator whose efforts had not resolved the dispute. "At this time I don't think any further action by me is appropriate," he said.

"UPS is a very important company to our country and there are a lot of employees there and I hope they'll go back to the table," Clinton told reporters during a meeting with business executives in the White House cabinet room on climate change.

Earlier Monday, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said he saw "no possibility" of Clinton ending the strike, saying the Taft-Hartley Act requires that such a strike must imperil the national health or safety before the president may step in.
The Teamsters union began a strike at UPS early Monday morning after negotiators failed to agree a new contract at the largest U.S. small package carrier.
UPS handles 12 million packages a day and employs 301,000 people in the United States, 185,000 of whom are represented by the Teamsters, including package sorters, loaders and drivers.
